# Michael Baker

CEO and Managing Director at Percheron Therapeutics Limited

Greater Melbourne Area (AU)

500 connections • 3,353 followers

## About

Dr Michael Baker actively advises and supports diverse biotechnology companies, leveraging an extensive track record of guiding complex drug development efforts across a wide range of therapeutic areas. With a career spanning executive leadership, venture capital, and elite scientific research, he bridges the gap between breakthrough science and commercial reality. Dr Michael Baker was previously the CEO & Managing Director of Arovella Therapeutics (ASX: ALA), and championed a strategic turnaround of the company from a small molecule reformulation-focused entity to a clinical-stage company developing personalised cell therapies for cancer patients. During his time at Arovella, Michael assembled and guided a world-class team spanning Australia, the US and the UK. He led the strategy development at Arovella, including in-licensing technologies from world-class universities and research institutes. He also led the team to manage pre-clinical studies, GMP manufacturing and clinical planning, which culminated in acceptance of the US FDA IND to start phase 1 clinical studies. During his tenure, he was also responsible for investor relations, raising capital and strategic partner engagement. Previously, Michael had a distinguished career as a research scientist, where his research led to numerous high-impact research publications. He completed his PhD in Biochemistry at La Trobe University, and his thesis received the Nancy Millis award for the best thesis for the faculty of Science Technology and Engineering. Michael completed his MBA at Melbourne Business School in 2018 and received an MBS award for Distinction.

Total Experience: 21 years and 10 months

As Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of Percheron Therapeutics (ASX: PER), I lead the strategic, clinical and corporate development of a biotechnology company focused on advancing novel immuno-oncology therapies and creating long-term value for shareholders. Our primary focus is accelerating the development of HMBD-002, a first-in-class monoclonal antibody targeting the immune checkpoint VISTA, while pursuing scientifically rational combination approaches, investigator-initiated studies and strategic partnerships that can efficiently generate meaningful clinical data. I bring a combination of scientific, investment and executive leadership experience to the role, having previously served as CEO and Managing Director of Arovella Therapeutics and worked within the Australian biotechnology venture capital sector. My passion lies in translating innovative science into clinical impact, building high-performing teams, and identifying opportunities that maximise the value of breakthrough technologies for patients and investors.

# Percheron Therapeutics Installs Arovella Veteran Baker as CEO, Roadshow Set for October

Percheron Therapeutics (ASX: PER) has confirmed Dr Michael Baker commenced as chief executive officer and managing director on 5 October, completing the…

 By Rachel Underwood · 5 October 2026 · 2 min read 

Percheron Therapeutics (ASX: PER) has confirmed Dr Michael Baker commenced as chief executive officer and managing director on 5 October, completing the leadership transition announced in August when Dr James Garner stepped down from the role.

Baker joins from Arovella Therapeutics (ASX: ALA), where he served as CEO and managing director and oversaw the company's pivot into cell therapy. He holds a PhD in biochemistry from La Trobe University and an MBA from Melbourne Business School, with prior experience at a biotechnology-focused venture capital fund. Baker's capital markets background arrives as Percheron moves toward further HMBD-002 trials.

The appointment places a capital markets-experienced executive at the helm as Percheron prepares for further clinical development of HMBD-002, a monoclonal antibody targeting the immune checkpoint regulator VISTA. The company completed a Phase I trial in advanced cancer patients demonstrating the drug was generally safe and well-tolerated, and has flagged plans for additional trials in calendar year 2026.

"His experience in drug development and capital markets will be a significant asset to the Company, and we feel confident that under his leadership the Company is well placed to unlock the full potential of its lead asset, HMBD-002," chair Dr Charmaine Gittleson said.

Baker said Percheron was "in an excellent position with a unique VISTA-targeting mAb that has demonstrated excellent safety data and has multiple cost-effective pathways to generate promising efficacy data."

The transition follows Bell Wire's August report on Garner's departure and Baker's appointment. Percheron's July quarterly disclosed A$4.05 million in cash with plans to restart clinical activities following drug batch clearance.

Baker will meet existing and prospective shareholders at an investor roadshow in Melbourne on 20 October, Sydney on 21 October, and Perth on 22–23 October.

# Percheron Therapeutics installs new CEO as Baker takes helm from Garner

Dr Michael Baker has formally commenced as chief executive officer and managing director of Percheron Therapeutics (ASX: PER), completing a leadership transition first announced in August as the…

FC

Fiona Calder Health & Biotech · 5 Oct 2026 · 2 min read

Dr Michael Baker has formally commenced as chief executive officer and managing director of Percheron Therapeutics (ASX: PER), completing a leadership transition first announced in August as the biotech prepares to advance its lead oncology asset through further clinical development.

The appointment, effective Monday, brings to Percheron a veteran of the Australian cell therapy sector. Baker most recently served as CEO and managing director of Arovella Therapeutics (ASX: ALA), where he repositioned the company from a legacy business into a cell therapy developer. He holds a PhD in biochemistry from La Trobe University and an MBA from Melbourne Business School, with prior experience at a biotechnology-focused venture capital fund.

The transition follows the departure of Dr James Garner, who stepped down from the CEO role as announced on 10 August 2026. Garner had overseen Percheron through a period that included the completion of a Phase 1 clinical trial for its lead program, HMBD-002, a monoclonal antibody targeting VISTA, an immune checkpoint regulator involved in suppressing anti-tumour immune responses.

## Investor roadshow planned

Baker will move quickly to meet the market. The company has scheduled an investor roadshow across Melbourne on 20 October, Sydney on 21 October, and Perth on 22 and 23 October, covering Percheron’s strategy, clinical development programs and near-term priorities.

The roadshow timing aligns with a period of renewed clinical activity for the company. In late July, Percheron confirmed receipt of a cleared drug batch and flagged a September restart for clinical work, positioning the company to advance HMBD-002 into further trials during calendar year 2026.

## The clinical program

HMBD-002 has completed a Phase 1 trial in patients with advanced cancer. The trial established the drug as generally safe and well-tolerated, providing the foundation for Percheron to pursue additional studies. VISTA-targeting therapies represent a less crowded area of immuno-oncology compared with PD-1 and CTLA-4 inhibitors, though the pathway remains earlier in clinical validation.

Chair Dr Charmaine Gittleson said the board was confident Baker’s experience in drug development and capital markets would help unlock the potential of HMBD-002.

“We are in an excellent position with a unique VISTA-targeting mAb that has demonstrated excellent safety data and has multiple cost-effective pathways to generate promising efficacy data,” Baker said. “I am committed to unlocking the value of our assets and generating value for all Percheron shareholders.”

## What it means

Baker brings a track record of repositioning ASX-listed biotechs, and the roadshow timing suggests the board is moving quickly on both clinical development and capital markets.

The investor roadshow later this month will be the first opportunity for shareholders to hear Baker’s strategic priorities directly; the next material catalyst is the advancement of HMBD-002 into further clinical trials, with the company targeting additional studies in calendar 2026.

- A new batch of HMBD-002 drug product has been manufactured and is ready for deployment in clinical trials.

The company has partnered with Vanderbilt Health in Nashville, Tennessee, to conduct this study as an investigator-sponsored study (IST), meaning the centre performs the majority of the work involved in executing the study. According to the filing, the IST structure has allowed Percheron to proceed with the clinical trial without incurring what the Chair described as prohibitive financial liabilities. The filing states the company looks forward to the study commencing recruitment in the near future.
